name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+40 partisan lean makes this one of the most Democratic districts in the country
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
Democratic nominee Chris Rabb heavily outraises independent Dennis Mahoney
Open seat carries minor uncertainty with incumbent Dwight Evans retiring
model.rationale: A D+40 Philadelphia seat with no Republican on the ballot and a massively better-funded Democratic nominee leaves essentially no path for the independent challenger; the baseline margin of 32.4 stands with only token adjustment for open-seat uncertainty.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or strong independent fundraising surge could narrow the margin, though not the likely winner.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Philadelphia's 3rd District is among the most Democratic seats in the nation, with a partisan lean of D+40. Dwight Evans is retiring, leaving an open seat, but the Democratic nominee, state representative Chris Rabb, faces only an independent, Dennis Mahoney, in the general election. Rabb has raised over $1.3 million with substantial outside support, while Mahoney has raised roughly $10,000 with no outside spending.

Prediction markets give the Democrat about a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a wide Democratic margin. The open seat adds a small amount of uncertainty, but the outcome is not in realistic doubt.
